# `particle_voice/nn/kernels/WGSLSourceMap.js`

> **Source:** `agi/particle_voice/nn/kernels/WGSLSourceMap.js`

WGSLSourceMap.js — Phase 1 ParticleNN kernel infrastructure. Generated-WGSL-line -> originating-chunk mapping. Kernels compose WGSL from named chunks (`ShaderComposer.js`) plus their own body; when the GPU compiler reports an error at line N, this turns that bare line number back into "which named chunk (or the kernel's own body) that line came from" — the JS source itself isn't line-mapped (these are template literals, not a separate compilation step), but chunk attribution is usually enough to know where to look.

## Classes

### `class WGSLSourceMap`

WGSLSourceMap.js — Phase 1 ParticleNN kernel infrastructure. Generated-WGSL-line -> originating-chunk mapping. Kernels compose WGSL from named chunks (`ShaderComposer.js`) plus their own body; when the GPU compiler reports an error at line N, this turns that bare line number back into "which named chunk (or the kernel's own body) that line came from" — the JS source itself isn't line-mapped (these are template literals, not a separate compilation step), but chunk attribution is usually enough to know where to look.

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor()` |  |
| `addSegment` | `addSegment(name, source)` | Append `source` as a named segment, returning it unchanged — call this in place of directly concatenating chunk sources while assembling a kernel's WGSL, so segment boundaries are tracked as a side effect. |
| `build` | `build()` | Combine every added segment's source into the final WGSL string, in the order they were added. |
| `resolve` | `resolve(lineNumber)` | Which segment (if any) contains `lineNumber` (1-indexed, as reported by `GPUCompilationMessage.lineNum`). |
| `totalLines` | `get totalLines()` |  |

## Notes & Examples

### Where this fits in the training loop

AGI runs an **observation → brain → action → reward** loop each tick: observations are gathered from the world, a brain maps them to actions, the rig applies motion, and rewards shape the next update.

**Example: Minimal training loop**
```js
import { Agent } from 'agi/core/Agent.js';
import { World } from 'agi/env/World.js';

const world = new World();
const agent = new Agent({
  brain: 'ppo',
  observationSpace: world.observationSpace,
  actionSpace: world.actionSpace
});

for (let step = 0; step < 10000; step++) {
  const obs = world.getObservation();      // Gather observations
  const action = agent.act(obs);            // Brain decides action
  const { reward, done } = world.step(action); // Apply action, get reward
  agent.learn(obs, action, reward);         // Update from experience
  
  if (done) world.reset();
}
```

**See also:** [AGI Training Guide](/agi/training-guide.md) · [AGI Architecture](/agi/architecture.md)
